say: Does one side of the face droop?
steps.quote: FACE: Ask the person to smile. Check if one side of the face droops.

say: Ask them to raise both arms.
steps.quote: ARMS: Ask the person to raise both arms. See if one arm drifts downward.

say: Ask them to repeat a simple sentence.
steps.quote: SPEECH: Ask the person to repeat a simple sentence. Check if words are slurred and if the sentence is repeated correctly.

say: This could be a stroke. Minutes matter.
Tell 911 when they last seemed normal.
steps.quote: If stroke is suspected, the EMS system should be activated immediately.

steps.sub: Don't drive them. Wait for EMS.
say: Stay with them. Don't drive them yourself.
If they stop responding, tell me.
steps.quote: TIME: If a person shows any of these symptoms, time is essential. Call 911 or the local emergency number.
steps.note: "Don't drive them yourself" is our routing advice (EMS can pre-alert a stroke center); it is not a guideline sentence. Reviewer: confirm you are comfortable with it.

steps.sub: Still call 911 if something is sudden or wrong.
say: No clear stroke signs right now.
If anything is sudden or wrong, call 911.
steps.quote: The use of a stroke recognition scale, such as the Face, Arms, Speech, Time (FAST) or Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale, is recommended to aid in the recognition of acute stroke in adults.
